headline: High-risk shared workspace and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure; CrewAI’s default isolation is none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest external data via APIs and MCP-style tool use, while CrewAI runs a shared-memory crew with no default self-isolation. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled content from aci outputs to influence CrewAI prompts or tool calls. The bridge is not proven by docs, so I rate it medium rather than high.
conditions: IF aci outputs untrusted text into a CrewAI task or memory slot
IF CrewAI agents treat upstream content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data separator in the handoff prompt
Strip HTML/markdown and code fences before passing outputs
Require provenance tags on all upstream content
Disable shared memory for untrusted tasks
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress. CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and can send tool data to model providers or configured integrations. If sensitive records are placed in the shared workspace, CrewAI can exfiltrate them through its default tool and model paths, so the blast radius is substantial.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF CRM, email, or support artifacts are stored in that workspace
IF CrewAI tools or model calls receive those files as context
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared directory
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
Disable file ingestion for CrewAI on sensitive runs
Rotate any exposed API keys after a test run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API-side actions, while CrewAI supports multiple instances with developer-defined shared state and host filesystem writes. Even though CrewAI cannot modify git state, both can still contend over the same files or external resources if orchestrated together. The overlap is real but not the high-severity git-lock case.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same working directory
IF the orchestrator shares mutable state between CrewAI instances
IF either agent updates the same CRM or spreadsheet record concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes to shared external systems
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Use idempotent update keys for CRM writes
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew and shared memory make it likely to treat upstream agent output as actionable context, while aci can generate CRM/email/calendar content and trigger integrations. If CrewAI acts on aci-produced facts without verification, errors can cascade into emails, calendar changes, or CRM updates. That is a default-dangerous pathway with potentially irreversible external actions.
conditions: IF CrewAI consumes aci output as task context or memory
IF CrewAI tools are configured to send email, update CRM, or schedule calendar events
IF no verification step checks aci-generated facts before action
mitigations: Require human approval before external actions
Add a verification agent that cross-checks facts
Log and diff all proposed outbound actions
Restrict CrewAI tools to read-only during testing
requires-engineering: implement action-gating policies

E_compliance.rationale: aci explicitly handles CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data, while CrewAI processes developer-passed crew data and can write the host filesystem. If regulated or customer data is placed into CrewAI’s workspace, retention and residency controls may diverge from aci’s upstream handling. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is passed from aci into CrewAI files or prompts
IF the host filesystem retention differs from the source system retention
IF the deployment stores data in a jurisdiction or vendor boundary not approved for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of CrewAI inputs
Set short retention on working directories
Document the data flow and residency boundary
Purge logs after each run
requires-engineering: add policy-based data-loss controls
